holidays.name: National Bikini Day
holidays.description: A salute to the tiny two-piece swimsuit that changed beach fashion forever. Celebrate with your favorite swimwear, a sunny spot, and no apologies about sand in unfortunate places.
holidays.origin: The modern bikini made its debut on July 5, 1946. French designer Louis Réard unveiled it at a Paris pool, and he named it after Bikini Atoll, where the United States had just conducted nuclear tests. He hoped it would cause an explosive reaction.
holidays.funFact: Réard couldn't find a professional model willing to wear his design, so he hired Micheline Bernardini, a nude dancer from the Casino de Paris, to debut it.

holidays.name: National Graham Cracker Day
holidays.description: A day to honor the humble honey-sweet cracker that holds s'mores together and props up cheesecake crusts. Snack on them plain, dunk them in milk, or build a campfire classic.
holidays.origin: The cracker is named for Sylvester Graham, a 19th-century minister and diet reformer. He promoted a bland whole-wheat diet that he believed would curb unruly impulses. The day is an unofficial food observance.
holidays.funFact: The original graham cracker was meant to be plain and austere, and it was a far cry from today's sugary versions. Graham thought bland food would promote moral living.

holidays.name: National Workaholics Day
holidays.description: A cheeky observance that nudges the overworked to look up from the laptop. It's an invitation to take stock of your work-life balance, then maybe close the inbox.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance with unclear origins. It's widely listed as a reminder to check in on healthy work habits rather than a celebration of overwork.
holidays.funFact: Despite the name, the day is usually pitched as a prompt to unplug, which makes it one of the few holidays that people are tempted to skip because they're too busy.
